**Grant Application: CalVIP Funding Request**

Sacramento's communities of color face disproportionate rates of gun violence, demanding culturally competent prevention. Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC) is a minority-owned social enterprise dedicated to empowering these communities through innovative gun safety education. Partnering with the Church of Legacy, we address critical needs.

Our signature *Gloxsie 21* cartoon IP engages youth with vital safety messages through relatable storytelling. Complementary AI education equips participants with future-ready skills, fostering critical thinking relevant to responsible technology use and community safety data analysis. Direct community workshops, hosted by Church of Legacy, provide hands-on training in safe gun storage, conflict de-escalation, and responsible ownership.

Our programs will demonstrably reduce accidental firearm injuries, increase safe storage practices, and empower youth and families with life-saving knowledge. We anticipate a measurable decrease in preventable gun-related incidents and an increase in community well-being and safety awareness across Sacramento.

As a minority-owned enterprise deeply rooted in Sacramento, GAFC offers unparalleled cultural competency and trust. Our bold name reflects our commitment to tackling uncomfortable truths with direct, effective solutions. Our trusted partnership with the Church of Legacy amplifies our reach and impact.

A CalVIP grant of $500,000 will enable GAFC to scale these vital programs, creating lasting change and safer futures in Sacramento's most vulnerable neighborhoods.
